title: Four moments, respectful words, and being ready to serve

say: Four moments, respectful words, and being ready to serve.
This is the video for module one of Customer Care and Respectful Communication.
Customer service is the task: selling the bread, plaiting the hair, sending the money.

panel.heading: Service is the task. Care is how
items: Care: how the person is treated

say: Customer care is how the person is treated while the task happens. Two shops can do the same task well, yet one customer leaves feeling respected and the other feeling like a nuisance.

panel.heading: Service is the task. Care is how
items: Care: how the person is treated

say: Care usually costs nothing, and it is fully in your hands. Let us see where it happens.

panel.heading: Service is the task. Care is how
items: Care: how the person is treated

say: Every visit, call or chat passes through four moments. A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.
For example, Ngozi runs a small salon in Enugu. Her regular customer Ada arrives for an appointment.

panel.heading: Score the four moments of a visit

say: Arrive. Ngozi is on the phone and nobody greets Ada for about five minutes. Score 0.

panel.heading: Score the four moments of a visit

say: Wait. Ngozi apologises, says honestly she needs 15 more minutes, and offers water and a seat. Score 2.

panel.heading: Score the four moments of a visit

say: Serve and pay. She agrees the style and price before starting, but talks loudly in a language Ada does not speak. Score 1.

panel.heading: Score the four moments of a visit

say: Leave. She thanks Ada but does not check whether she is happy with the edges. Score 1.

panel.heading: Score the four moments of a visit

say: That is 4 out of 8, and the weakest moment is the greeting. Ngozi's one free fix: whoever is nearest the door says, welcome, I'll be with you soon. Keep one rule for two weeks before moving on.

panel.heading: Score the four moments of a visit
panel.rule: Score each moment 0, 1 or 2. Fix the weakest first.

say: In most Nigerian communities, the greeting is not a small thing. Say good morning, good afternoon, or good evening. A plain yes, or what do you want, starts badly.

panel.heading: Greetings and titles that fit
items: Greet first, by time of day
Add Ma or Sir for adults you don't know
Local language only if you speak it well
Let the customer offer a hand first

say: Greet first, and add Ma or Sir, especially for elders. Avoid words like this woman or baby with adults you do not know well.

say: A greeting in the customer's language can feel warm, but if you do not speak it well, use polite English or Pidgin instead of guessing.

say: Some customers prefer not to shake hands. A smile and a nod are always safe.

say: And once you know a regular customer's name, use it. People warm up when they are remembered.

say: Listen to these: wait there, price is fixed, next. They are quick, but they sound cold.

panel.heading: From curt to respectful
right: Please give me two minutes, Sir.
Sorry, I can't reduce this one.

say: Each respectful version keeps the same facts, but adds a polite word, a reason or a time, and where possible an alternative.
I'm sorry, I can't reduce this one. It's already our lowest price. I can show you a smaller size. You still say no, but the customer keeps her dignity.
Tone matters too. Rushing, shouting or a flat voice all sound rude, especially on calls and voice notes.

panel.heading: From curt to respectful
right: Please give me two minutes, Sir.

say: Most rudeness from sellers is not planned. It comes from tiredness, hunger or a bad moment just before. So notice your own state first.

panel.heading: A ten-second breathing pause
items: Stop. Put down what you are holding
This is about the situation, not me
Greet as if it is the first customer

say: Stop, and put down what you are holding.

panel.heading: A ten-second breathing pause
items: Stop. Put down what you are holding
This is about the situation, not me
Greet as if it is the first customer

say: Breathe in slowly through your nose while you count to 4. Breathe out through your mouth while you count to 6. Repeat two or three times.

panel.heading: A ten-second breathing pause
items: Stop. Put down what you are holding
This is about the situation, not me
Greet as if it is the first customer

say: Say to yourself: this is about the situation, not about me. An angry customer is usually angry at a late order or a long queue.

panel.heading: A ten-second breathing pause
items: Stop. Put down what you are holding
This is about the situation, not me
Greet as if it is the first customer

say: Then greet the customer as if they are the first of the day. Plan short breaks too, with water and something to eat.

say: Do this one-minute check before you open. You have eaten and had water. Your phone is away. Your price list is visible. Your path to the exit is clear. Your cash is out of sight. And you have agreed a help signal with a neighbour.
Never argue with someone who is threatening you. Step back, call for help, and let the item or money go. No sale is worth your safety.
To remember. Watch the four moments and score them to find your weak link. Use a polite word, a reason or time, and an alternative.
Pause and breathe before a difficult customer. And your safety always comes first.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Arrive, wait, serve and pay, leave
Polite word, reason or time, alternative
Pause and breathe before a hard customer
Your safety comes before any sale
